title: Capability security, in 60 seconds

scenes.title: Code can ask. Permission decides.
scenes.subtitle: Client agent → gateway → compiler with protected functions
scenes.narration: A client agent sends a program to the compiler through the gateway. Ordinary computation runs freely. Protected functions need permission.

scenes.title: Share one action. Keep the credential.
scenes.subtitle: The owner grants an exact language and function on a connection.
scenes.narration: The connection owner grants a user specific language functions, such as saving to the item bank. The provider credential stays inside the broker.

scenes.title: Check the whole chain before it runs.
scenes.subtitle: Preflight is side-effect free. Every stage must be admitted.
scenes.narration: The gateway preflights every compiler stage. Policy checks the entire chain. One denied function blocks the run before any stage executes.

scenes.title: Mint authority for this exact call.
scenes.subtitle: Policy issues the capability. The compiler presents it to Broker.
scenes.narration: Policy issues the compiler a capability: single use, valid for sixty seconds at most, bound to the function and exact arguments.

scenes.title: Check permission at the point of use.
scenes.subtitle: Broker verifies the token and asks Policy before each effect.
scenes.narration: Broker verifies the capability and checks live permission before each effect. Active grants allow the provider call. Revoked permission blocks the next effect.

scenes.title: Record the outcome. Make retries safe.
scenes.subtitle: Same operation ID + fresh authorization → recorded receipt, no repeated write.
scenes.narration: A durable receipt records the outcome. Retrying the same operation returns its receipt without repeating the write. The agent gets results, never credentials.

scope: Conceptual explanation of the repository model, not a production conformance audit. No transactionality, provider exactly-once guarantee, or rollback is implied. Live checks prevent the next effect; they cannot undo a dispatched operation.
